false_belief: A heavier or faster body exerts a greater force on a lighter one during an interaction.
observable_evidence: Learner assigns a larger contact force to the more massive or faster object in a collision or contact problem.
common_argument: Obviously the truck hits the scooter harder than the scooter hits the truck — just look at the damage.
repair_criteria: Learner states the interaction forces are equal in magnitude and explains the different outcomes through different masses producing different accelerations.
debate_problem: A loaded truck collides head-on with a scooter. During the impact, which vehicle exerts the larger force on the other?
transfer_contexts: Tug of war between unequal teams
correct_model: Interaction forces between two bodies are always equal in magnitude and opposite in direction; the lighter body suffers more because equal force on smaller mass gives larger acceleration.
